findings.title: Vault creators can not withdraw their fees without being recursively charged (vault and program) fees on their own fees which causes permanent loss of funds
findings.description:
1. **Description:** Vault and program fee wallet owners (such as vault creators or admins) are subject to the same withdrawal fees when attempting to withdraw their accrued fees, leading to recursive fee deductions. Each withdrawal attempt results in a portion of the fee being re-deducted as both vault and program fees, preventing full withdrawal without multiple recursive transactions.

2. **Cause:** The system applies withdrawal fees uniformly to all withdrawals, including those initiated by the fee wallets themselves. There is no exemption logic for fee wallet withdrawals, and fee changes only take effect in the next epoch, making it impossible to temporarily disable fees for self-withdrawals.

3. **Exploitation:** An attacker is not required here, as the protocol itself enforces the fee deduction. However, a malicious or misconfigured admin could exploit this design to drain fee wallets over time. More critically, legitimate fee wallet owners are forced into a cycle where each withdrawal incurs additional fees, effectively locking a portion of their funds.

4. **Impact:** This leads to permanent loss of funds for fee wallet owners due to overpayment of program fees (e.g., 25% higher than expected in the POC). Additionally, full withdrawal is severely delayed—up to 42 epochs (84 days) in the example—constituting a denial-of-service condition and increasing transaction costs.
